title: Normalized coefficient encoding and a fixed compactification
statement: For a finite discrete commutative ring A, any family E of normalized Encodings from [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding], any scheme morphism f:X->Y, and any specified compactification c of f, there is a natural isomorphism from CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c followed by (E Y).fixedDerived to (E X).fixedDerived followed by the fixed ModuleCat(ULift A) rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification c. Both functors use the very same c; no alternative compactification or completion is used.

proof.text: Reuse encodingPushforwardNatIso, the proved private natural pushforward comparison in the module of [lem-pe-finite-discrete-encoding-pullback-fixed]. It identifies the actual normalized scalar actions using [lem-sf-finite-discrete-encoding-naturality]. Conjugate it by the encoding equivalences and apply uniqueness of left adjoints to the inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions. This produces a natural pullback comparison, rather than only an objectwise isomorphism.

For an open immersion j, conjugate the pullback comparison by the encoding equivalences. Compose each encoding adjunction with the appropriate extension-by-zero/pullback adjunction. Their right adjoints are naturally isomorphic, so leftAdjointUniq gives j!internal followed by E_T naturally isomorphic to E_U followed by j!fixed.

For pushforward, apply rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso to the exact target encoding, rightDerivedFunctorNatIso to the underived pushforward comparison, and mapDerivedCategoryCompRightDerivedFunctorIso to the source encoding. The source encoding preserves K-injectives because it is an additive equivalence, by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. For extension by zero, derive the exact natural comparison using mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso on its two sides. These are the separately derived factors in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification].

Whisker the derived pushforward comparison by D(c.i!), reassociate, whisker the derived extension-by-zero comparison by R(c.g*), and reassociate again. The resulting natural isomorphism is exactly the displayed comparison, using E(c.Z) at the intermediate scheme and the original compactification c throughout.

lean.statement:
theorem encoding_compactification [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A]
    (E : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Encoding A T)
    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification f) :
    Nonempty (CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c ⋙
        (E Y).fixedDerived.functor ≅
      (E X).fixedDerived.functor ⋙
        rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)) c)
